name: Ground cherry

schedule.notes: Treat like tomatoes — wait for warm soil and reliably warm nights.
Fruits drop to the ground in their husks when ripe — just pick them up daily.

harvest.cues: Husks dry and paper-bag tan; fruits drop on their own. Inner fruit golden-yellow. Don't pick before drop — they're not ripe.
harvest.storageNotes: In husks at room temp 2 to 3 months. The husk preserves them. Husked: fridge 1 to 2 weeks.

varieties.name: Aunt Molly's
varieties.notes: Pineapple-mango flavor when fully ripe. Heirloom favorite.

varieties.name: Cossack Pineapple
varieties.notes: Strong pineapple notes. Slightly larger fruits.

notes: Self-seeds aggressively — one season's volunteers can carpet the bed next year. Sprawling 2 to 3 ft plants; let them run or cage loosely. Great in jam, pies, or eaten by the handful warm from the husk.
